scope: Proposition 2.3 (Canonical and grand-canonical limits) of the manuscript “A continuum temperature singularity for a radial pair potential” (preprints/A-continuum-temperature-singularity-for-a-radial-pair-potential-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 228 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d3c00f7387c84c30), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every β > 0 and d ≥ 0 there is a finite limit Hφ(β, d) = − lim L→∞ n/L3→d log ZL,n(β) tL3 , Hφ(β, 0) = 0. (2.7) Extend Hφ(β, d) by +∞ for d < 0. It is closed and convex in d, and finite and concave in β for every d ≥ 0. Moreover, Hφ(β, d) ≥ βκ t d2 − βB0 t d + d log d − d t (d ≥ 0). (2.8) Let Ω = (0, ∞) × R, with coordinates (β, h), and define Ξφ L(β, h) = X n≥0 ethn ZL,n(β). Then the finite convex pressure is Qφ(β, h) = lim L→∞ log Ξφ L(β, h) tL3 = sup d≥0 {hd − Hφ(β, d)}. (2.9) The convergence is uniform on compact subsets of Ω, and Hφ(β, d) = sup h∈R {hd − Qφ(β, h)} (d ∈ R). (2.10) The bounds above use the same constants for the entire class (2.3) with the chosen t.
